item.title: TRESS forecasting model retains timestamped recent events for efficient predictions
item.description:
TRESS forecasting model retains timestamped recent events for efficient predictions

A new forecasting model called TRESS (Timestamped Recent Events and Statistical Summaries) addresses the challenge that a fixed number of recent observations may span minutes for one variable and days for another, while earlier measurements can still reveal whether the latest value is unusual for that variable.

🔍 Overview

The proposed model retains the latest observations at their original times and summarises the full history of each variable. For a given set of variables and event budget, this representation stays the same size as the record grows.

🧩 How it works

  • A query-conditioned event lifting module weights deviations from the latest value according to the age of each observation and the forecast horizon.
  • A channel-specific decoder combines the resulting features with historical statistics and a summary shared across variables to predict a correction to the latest value.

⚙️ Key details

  • TRESS retains 8 to 16 observations per variable.
  • On all four benchmarks compared, TRESS records the lowest mean test MSE and MAE among the methods tested.
  • Serving 32 successive query times from one encoded history reduces CPU inference time by a factor of 2.12 to 2.60 across the four datasets.

🚀 Availability

The code for the model is available at the URL provided in the source material.

#Forecasting #MachineLearning #TimeSeries #DeepLearning #Efficiency

Source: TRESS: A Fixed-Size History Representation for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

item.title: BATMoS Improves Video Diffusion Efficiency via Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation
item.description:
BATMoS Improves Video Diffusion Efficiency via Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation

Researchers have introduced BATMoS (Budget Aware Temporal Mixture of Strategies), a method that allocates classifier-free guidance computations more efficiently across the denoising trajectory in video diffusion models. The approach achieves near-full-guidance quality with fewer denoiser evaluations by reusing cached guidance during low-magnitude timesteps.

🔍 Overview

A new paper submitted on 17 Nov 2026 in Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition presents BATMoS, a budget-aware guidance allocation strategy for video diffusion models. The work demonstrates that inference budget effectiveness depends critically on where computation is spent along the denoising trajectory, with VBench total scores spanning 4.80 points across eight equal-budget configurations.

🧩 How It Works

The core insight is that guidance evaluations are not equally valuable across diffusion time. BATMoS routes between fresh classifier-free guidance and cached guidance using a single pretrained denoiser:

  • A magnitude-based temporal rule assigns guidance reuse to low-magnitude blocks and reserves fresh guidance for the remaining blocks
  • A single integer controls the computation budget
  • The resulting schedule requires no additional router training or per-budget threshold search

⚙️ Key Details

Evaluation on CogVideoX-2B with 4,720 videos per configuration across all sixteen official VBench dimensions shows:

  • BATMoS achieves the highest total score among eight allocation policies
  • It comes within 0.10 points of full classifier-free guidance using 20% fewer branch evaluations
  • When composed with feature reuse, computation reduces from 80 to 62 effective branch evaluations with a 0.11-point decrease in total score

💡 Why It Matters

These findings establish temporal guidance allocation as a practical mechanism for extracting more generation quality from a fixed inference budget, without requiring model retraining or complex routing mechanisms.

#VideoDiffusion #Efficiency #GuidanceAllocation #CogVideoX #VBench

Source: BATMoS: Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation for Efficient Video Diffusion

item.title: LLM Compression Research: A New Suite of Survey Papers
item.description:
LLM Compression Research: A New Suite of Survey Papers

A newly curated set of AI research papers focuses on techniques to compress large language models and accelerate their training and inference.

🔍 Overview

  • The collection aggregates several survey papers covering a wide range of efficiency‑oriented topics in large language models.
  • Papers are organized by year in collapsible blocks, newest first; the current year is expanded by default.

🧩 How it Works

  • Each paper provides a comprehensive review of existing methods for a particular sub‑field such as model routing, distillation, memory management, and low‑precision training.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Dynamic Model Routing and Cascading for Efficient LLM Inference
  • On‑Policy Distillation for Large Language Models

  • KV Cache Compression Techniques
  • Measurement Study of LLM Applications on Mobile Devices
  • Knowledge Distillation and Dataset Distillation of Large Language Models

item.title: Researchers Develop COMPACTIONBENCH and APEC to Reduce AI Coding Costs
item.description:
Researchers Develop COMPACTIONBENCH and APEC to Reduce AI Coding Costs

A new study reveals that while fewer than 8% of coding sessions require context compaction, these sessions account for 44% of total AI processing costs. To address this, researchers have introduced tools to optimize long-running coding tasks.

🧩 How it works

Researchers developed two primary solutions to manage context compaction more efficiently:

  • COMPACTIONBENCH: A benchmark designed to evaluate context compaction during long-running coding tasks.
  • APEC: A method that prepares summaries in the background, preventing the interruption of an agent’s work.

⚙️ Key details

Evaluations of the APEC method demonstrate measurable improvements in efficiency for coding agents:

Metric Improvement
Coding Performance Improved
Costs Reduced by up to 25.4%
Execution Time Reduced by 9.6%

#AI #Coding #MachineLearning #Efficiency

Source: Microsoft Research Focus – Edition #98 - Microsoft Research

🚀 MiniMax-M2: The Future of Efficient AI Coding and Agentic Workflows

Redefining efficiency for AI agents with a compact, fast, and cost-effective approach

🌟 Highlights

MiniMax-M2 represents a revolutionary leap in AI model efficiency, delivering Mini size with Max performance for coding and agentic workflows. This compact powerhouse features 230 billion total parameters with only 10 billion active parameters, making it a game-changer for developers seeking sophisticated AI capabilities without the computational overhead.

Key Achievements ⭐

  • 🏆 #1 Global Ranking: Composite score ranks #1 among open-source models globally according to Artificial Analysis benchmarks
  • 💡 Superior Intelligence: Highly competitive performance across mathematics, science, instruction following, coding, and agentic tool use
  • ⚡ Advanced Coding: Engineered for end-to-end developer workflows with excellence in multi-file edits, coding-run-fix loops, and test-validated repairs
  • 🤖 Agent Performance: Plans and executes complex, long-horizon toolchains across shell, browser, retrieval, and code runners
  • 🎯 Efficient Design: 10 billion activated parameters deliver lower latency, cost, and higher throughput

Performance comparison across various AI models and benchmarks

⚙️ Why Activation Size Matters

By maintaining activations around 10B parameters, MiniMax-M2 streamlines the plan → act → verify loop in agentic workflows:

🏁 Conclusion

MiniMax-M2 represents a paradigm shift in AI model design, proving that exceptional performance doesn’t require massive computational overhead. With its 10 billion active parameters delivering frontier-level coding and agentic capabilities, it offers the perfect balance of efficiency and intelligence for modern development workflows.

Whether you’re building complex multi-step agents, developing sophisticated coding assistants, or implementing intelligent automation, MiniMax-M2 provides a cost-effective, deployment-friendly solution without compromising on quality. The model’s impressive benchmark performance across coding, mathematics, and agentic tasks, combined with its efficient resource utilization, makes it an ideal choice for organizations seeking to implement AI-powered solutions at scale.

The open-source availability and multiple deployment options ensure that developers can integrate MiniMax-M2 into their existing infrastructure seamlessly, marking a significant step forward in democratizing advanced AI capabilities.
